---
title: "Standardize Specimen Records"
format: html
---

## Overview

The `barroso_std()` function is the primary tool in the `barRoso` package for performing full data cleaning and standardization of biodiversity specimen records. It is designed to process raw data from herbaria, virtual repositories, and field collections, ensuring harmonized fields across taxonomic, geographic, and collector-related information.

## Key Features

- Normalize collector names and collection numbers
- Normalize determiner names (`identifiedBy`)
- Standardize geographic fields like country, state, and locality
- Harmonize taxonomic names including family, genus, and species
- Clean and normalize type status
- Optionally remove unvouchered or duplicate records
- Support for multilingual column names (e.g., Portuguese, Spanish)

## Usage

```r
library(barRoso)

df <- read.csv("raw_herbarium_data.csv")

standardized_df <- barroso_std(df,
                               unvouchered = TRUE,
                               delunkcoll = FALSE,
                               flag_missid = TRUE,
                               flag_duplicates = TRUE,
                               rm_duplicates = FALSE,
                               index_herbariorum = TRUE,
                               colname_recordedBy = "recordedBy",
                               colname_recordNumber = "recordNumber",
                               colname_identifiedBy = "identifiedBy",
                               colname_country = "country",
                               colname_stateProvince = "stateProvince",
                               colname_county = "county",
                               colname_municipality = "municipality",
                               colname_locality = "locality",
                               colname_collectionCode = "collectionCode",
                               colname_institutionCode = "institutionCode",
                               colname_typeStatus = "typeStatus",
                               colname_family = "family",
                               colname_genus = "genus",
                               colname_specificEpithet = "specificEpithet",
                               rm_original_column = TRUE)
```

## Arguments

- `...`: A data frame or list of data frames with raw biodiversity records
- `unvouchered`: Remove records of wood, seed, fruit, pollen and spirit collections (e.g. `INPAw`, `INPA-Carpoteca`, `BHZBcarpo`), and observations without a specimen (`basisOfRecord` like `HUMAN_OBSERVATION`), before the herbarium codes are standardized
- `delunkcoll`: Optionally delete records with unknown collectors
- `flag_duplicates`, `rm_duplicates`: Detect and optionally remove duplicates
- `index_herbariorum`: Check collection codes against the API of [Index Herbariorum](https://sweetgum.nybg.org/science/ih/), always keeping the original codes (default: `TRUE`)
- `rm_original_column`: Remove original (uncleaned) fields after standardization

## Collector and determiner names

Collector names (`recordedBy`) are standardized with `std_recordedBy()` into initials followed by the surname, and additional collectors are moved to a new column `addCollector` (or stored as `"et al."` when there are more than two collectors). Determiner names (`identifiedBy`) are standardized with `std_identifiedBy()`, using the same rules, but all determiners are kept in the same cell. The original columns are kept with the suffix `Original`.

| Original | Standardized |
|---|---|
| `Cardoso, D.B.O.S.` | `D. B. O. S. Cardoso` |
| `Padgurschi, MCG` | `M. C. G. Padgurschi` |
| `Martius, CFP von` | `C. F. P. von Martius` |
| `Uribe Uribe AL` | `A. L. Uribe-Uribe` |
| `Dusén` | `Dusén` |
| `A. Gómez Pompa, A. J. Sharp & P. Hernández` | `A. Gómez Pompa` (`addCollector`: `et al.`) |
| `H.C. de Lima, C.A. Cid Ferreira, J. Guedes;F. Neves` | `H. C. Lima` (`addCollector`: `et al.`) |
| `Col. Richard Henry Beddome` | `R. H. Beddome` |
| `Warren Douglas Stevens, B. A. Krukoff Curator of Central American Botany` | `W. D. Stevens` |
| `236-6队` | `Dui` (`recordNumber`: `236-6`, or the number already there) |
| `[data not captured]`, `[see remarks]`, `-`, `?`, empty cells | `NA` |
| `Lobato, LC; Soares, CRA; Silva, CA` (determiners) | `L. C. Lobato, C. R. A. Soares & C. A. Silva` |
| `R.Barneby (NY) 1994-06` (determiner) | `R. Barneby` |
| `-`, `?` (determiners) | `NA` |

Chinese names written in Chinese characters (e.g. 丁广奇、余莲) or as unicode escapes, as in some GBIF downloads (e.g. `<U+674E><U+5149><U+7167>`, 李光照), are converted into Latin names as Chinese authors cite themselves in publications: initials of the given name followed by the family name, e.g. `G. Z. Li`, `T. S. Yi` (易婷双) and `R. Zhang` (张荣). Family names of two characters (e.g. `Ouyang`) and family names with a special reading (e.g. 曾, `Zeng`) are also handled, and names of teams or groups (e.g. 植被组, vegetation group) are kept in full. When the name is also written in Latin, e.g. `K.C.Yang 楊國禎` or `Peng, Ching-I (彭鏡毅)`, the Latin name is kept (`K. C. Yang`, `C.-I. Peng`).

Identifiers like `(Wikidata Q5850623)`, given names in lowercase (`katherine Bravo`) and abbreviations like `Edm.Pereira` are also cleaned, and names of teams and herbaria (e.g. `Equipe do Jardim Botânico de Brasília`, `Belem Herbarium`) are kept as they are.

## Herbarium acronyms

Herbarium acronyms (`collectionCode`) are standardized with `std_collection()` into the acronyms of [Index Herbariorum](https://sweetgum.nybg.org/science/ih/), using regular expressions rather than a list of every code:

| Original `collectionCode` | `institutionCode` or `catalogNumber` | Standardized |
|---|---|---|
| `Tropicos`, `MO-Duplicates` | `NY` | `NY` (the herbarium of the specimen) |
| `Botany`, `Herbarium`, `Vascular Plants` | `catalogNumber` `U.1317533` | `U` |
| (missing, GenBank voucher) | `catalogNumber` `D. Cardoso 2118 (HUEFS)` | `HUEFS` |
| `F-Seedplants`, `BHCB-Fanerogamas`, `R-Tipos`, `UIS-H` | | `F`, `BHCB`, `R`, `UIS` |
| `BSMvplantscoll`, `NL-Botany`, `CJBG-G-DC` | | `M`, `L`, `G-DC` |
| `Herbario INPA`, `Herbario Nacional de Costa Rica (CR)` | | `INPA`, `CR` |
| (missing) | `Instituto Florestal`, `Unicamp` | `SPSF`, `UEC` |
| `Observations`, `Dados de Pesquisa SISBio`, `Ecopetrol S.A` | | `NA` |

Codes of wood collections, like `INPAw`, are kept.

By default (`index_herbariorum = TRUE`), the standardized codes are then checked against all herbaria of Index Herbariorum, which are downloaded at once and kept during the R session:

- Codes found get the spelling of Index Herbariorum, e.g. `UnB` into `UNB`.
- Codes not found are looked for by the full name of the institution in the original `collectionCode` or `institutionCode`, when the name belongs to a single herbarium, as universities may have several.
- The code of Index Herbariorum goes into `collectionCode`, and `institutionCode` is not changed.
- The original code is always kept in `collectionCodeOriginal`, even with `rm_original_column = TRUE`.
- The new column `institutionName` has the name of the institution, and the new column `indexHerbariorum` is `FALSE` for codes not found, which are left as they were for checking.

The regular expressions remain the first step, as dirty codes like `F-Seedplants` or `Tropicos` are not in Index Herbariorum. The check needs internet access; if the API cannot be reached, a warning is given and the codes are not checked. Use `index_herbariorum = FALSE` to work offline.

## Places

Countries, states, counties and municipalities are standardized with `std_place()`, e.g. `BRASIL` into `Brazil` and `BA` into `Bahia`. Words for municipality are removed from `county` and `municipality`, leaving just the name, e.g. `Manaus Mun.`, `Mun. de Castelo` and `Município de Mucugê` into `Manaus`, `Castelo` and `Mucugê`. Country codes become names, e.g. `BR` and `GY` into `Brazil` and `Guyana`. Missing countries are taken from the Brazilian state (e.g. `Bahia`), from a country name at the start or end of the locality (e.g. `Rio Negro, Brasil`), or from other records with the same state and county (e.g. `Amazonas`, `Manaus`); names shared by several countries, like the state `Amazonas` alone, are left empty. Missing municipalities are taken from the county, as GBIF keeps the municipalities of Brazil in `county`. Localities all in upper case get just the first letter of each word in upper case, e.g. `ESTR. UBAITUBA / MARÁU AO KM 54 .` into `Estr. Ubaituba/Maráu ao Km 54.`, keeping prepositions in lowercase and road codes (`BR-316`), acronyms (`ESALQ`) and compass points (`10 Km NE de`) in upper case.

The final data frame is sorted by species, `recordedBy` and `recordNumber`. All records of a block of duplicates stay together under the most frequent name of the block, e.g. a duplicate identified as `Ormosia ruddiana` goes with its three duplicates identified as `Ormosia amazonica`, in the place of the latter species.

The function `barroso_std()` does not check geographic coordinates. Use [`std_coordinates()`](/articles/fix_flag_coordinates.qmd) for that.

## Output

Returns a cleaned and fully standardized data frame ready for:

- Reconciliation and deduplication
- Taxonomic and biogeographic analysis
- Herbarium label generation workflows

## Notes

- Uses dynamic regular expressions for name harmonization rather than static dictionaries
- Optimized for scalability and flexible input schema
- Recommended to run before calling downstream functions like `barroso_flag_duplicates()` or `barroso_labels()`

## Example

```r
cleaned_data <- barroso_std(df,
                            colname_country = "pais",
                            colname_stateProvince = "estado",
                            rm_duplicates = TRUE)
```

For a complete list of supported fields, refer to the function documentation with `?barroso_std`.
